paper.title: AutoDroid: LLM-powered Task Automation in Android
paper.central_claim: AutoDroid handles arbitrary tasks on any Android app without manual effort by combining LLM commonsense with app-specific knowledge from automated exploration (HTML-style UI prompting, exploration-based memory injection, query optimisation); authors report 90.9% action accuracy and a 71.3% task "success"/completion rate with GPT-4, above GPT-4-powered baselines.
paper.scope_as_measured: DroidTask: 158 tasks, 13 F-Droid apps explored offline by the system itself; teacher-forced matching against one annotated trace per task; completion-determination step excluded from completion rate.

missing_sections: Figures 6–9 are images; Figure 7/8 magnitudes (completion by steps, memory ablation) not recoverable from text. v4 has no appendix.

signatures.object: LLM next-action prompt for an Android GUI state
signatures.information: Android view tree rendered as 5-tag HTML; app memory from offline random exploration of the same app (privileged structural access, no screenshots)
signatures.operation: retrieve top-k simulated tasks by embedding similarity; inject onclick navigation hints and UI-function table into prompt; auto-scroll merging; prune/merge equivalent nodes
signatures.output: element id + action type/value (+ risk confirmation flag)
signatures.conditions: apps must be explorable offline; random exploration must reach needed screens; LLM summaries must be correct
signatures.selection_rule: similarity retrieval; shortcut when sim > gamma (gamma, k unreported)
signatures.later_use: DroidTask tasks on the same 13 apps
signatures.claimed_effect: higher action accuracy and completion, fewer tokens/calls
signatures.failure_boundary: alternative valid paths scored wrong (O05); completion detection errors; unseen apps untested

signatures.information: UTG-derived (state, action) pairs + GPT-4 zero-shot-CoT rationales given the correct action, plus MoTiF input/completion slice
signatures.operation: SFT on synthesised rationale pairs (no quality filter)
signatures.failure_boundary: No-CoT variant collapses to 20.6%; single 7B backbone

retained_chain.reason: Static one-time offline preparation (memory, SFT); no outcome-based selection/acceptance of changes, no retained-improvement claim. Both seats agree.

gap.author_gap: Manual demonstrations/rewards do not scale; prompt-only LLM agents lack app-specific knowledge; raw UI trees are long; LLM queries are costly.
gap.checked_gap: Real and concrete (deep-navigation example, 625→339 tokens). Lineage limited to LLM-framework (Wang 2023) and META-GUI; neighbours not pinned in the pack.
gap.residue: Whether exploration memory helps on apps not explored before deployment, and whether offline trace agreement predicts live completion.

expectations.text: Report online success on AndroidWorld for mobile-agent claims, not only offline AndroidControl/AITW step metrics
expectations.applies_when: an empirical claim that a method improves task success of an Android/mobile GUI agent
expectations.reason: Decided for son55. Mobile-agent claim with no online/executed success at all; authors explicitly withhold real-system results (O04). AndroidWorld postdates v1 (era note), but the expectation’s substance—online success, not only offline step metrics—is unmet, not partial.

expectations.text: Compare GUI online-RL methods against DigiRL, WebRL, filtered BC / AWR and an SFT-only model trained on the same data
expectations.applies_when: a claim that an RL algorithm (online, offline-to-online, semi-online or model-based) improves a GUI/web agent
expectations.reason: sol only; accepted: no RL algorithm claimed.

expectations.text: Validate an LLM/VLM success judge or outcome reward model against human labels on trajectories from agents not used to build it (agreement/accuracy, plus the resulting success-rate gap)
expectations.applies_when: a method that uses an LLM/VLM judge, ORM or reflector to label trajectory success for evaluation, filtering or reward
expectations.reason: sol only; accepted: success is trace matching, not an LLM judge; the risk detector (P/R reported) is not the evaluator.

expectations.text: Do not rest an agent capability claim on offline step accuracy (AndroidControl, Multimodal-Mind2Web, GUI Odyssey) alone; add an online benchmark or show the offline metric predicts online success
expectations.applies_when: a claim of improved agent capability measured with offline, teacher-forced step metrics
expectations.reason: [both seats agree] sol: 71.3% is sequence matching on provided UI sequence; neither executable end-state nor offline-online correlation. | son55: The capability claim (71.3% "success rate") rests on offline teacher-forced step/trace matching with a single annotated path; no argument that the metric predicts live success.

expectations.text: Report mean and spread over at least 3 runs (or confidence intervals) for online benchmark numbers
expectations.applies_when: an empirical comparison on an online/live benchmark (OSWorld, AndroidWorld, WebArena, Online-Mind2Web) where LLM sampling and environment noise vary across runs
expectations.reason: [both seats agree] sol: Central benchmark is offline; latency alone has 10 repeats. Absence of task repeated seeds/CI still informs statistics by ordinary sampling reliability, not a false claim of violated online protocol. | son55: Defined for online/live benchmarks; this paper reports offline trace matching. Statistical weakness (single run, temperature sensitivity of 2-4 points) is instead scored under E.statistics.

expectations.text: Compare agents at an equal, stated max-step budget (e.g. OSWorld 15 vs 50 steps), and report steps used / budget exhaustion
expectations.applies_when: a comparison of agent success where methods or baselines may run with different step caps
expectations.reason: Decided for son55. Teacher-forced per-step evaluation has no agent-loop step cap; sol’s concern (shortcut accounting conditioned on correct cases) is real but belongs to E.cost and is recorded there.

expectations.text: Report screenshot-only and accessibility-tree/DOM-augmented settings separately; a11y-tree availability changes results and reverses across models
expectations.applies_when: a comparison of GUI agents whose observation spaces may differ
expectations.reason: [both seats agree] sol: Structure-based setting clearly disclosed, but baseline sees visible leaves whereas AutoDroid also auto-scrolls and merges; comparison not equal-information. | son55: The observation space (Android tree as HTML) is stated and the main baseline uses the same modality, but no screenshot or tree-plus-screenshot setting is reported, so modality effects are not separated.

expectations.text: Report results across backbone sizes (e.g. 7B and 32B/72B), since gains from GUI data/RL recipes shrink with model size
expectations.applies_when: a claim that a training recipe generalises across policy backbones
expectations.reason: son55 only; accepted: memory tested on Vicuna-7B/GPT-3.5/GPT-4; SFT recipe on a single 7B model.

expectations.text: Stratify online success by human reference step count (difficulty) and audit failure causes
expectations.applies_when: a new benchmark or a claim about long-horizon GUI task capability
expectations.reason: son55 only; accepted: completion vs steps plotted (image), 20 failures categorised, no total-failure denominator.

expectations.text: Compare a synthetic-trajectory recipe against an instruction-first / task-driven synthesis baseline with the same executor and similar data size
expectations.applies_when: a claim that an exploration-first, reverse or world-model data-synthesis method yields better GUI training data
expectations.reason: son55 only; accepted: exploration-derived synthesis is never compared with instruction-first synthesis at equal data.

expectations.text: Show a data-scaling curve (fraction or count of synthetic samples vs downstream score) and say where it saturates
expectations.applies_when: a claim that synthetic GUI grounding, transition or trajectory data improves agents
expectations.reason: son55 only; accepted: no data-scaling curve for app-specific SFT data.

expectations.text: Separate synthesis/exploration environments from evaluation (held-out apps/sites, filtered test queries) and report out-of-distribution transfer
expectations.applies_when: a claim that self-generated tasks, explored transitions, memory or synthesised environments improve benchmark success
expectations.reason: Decided for son55. Exploration environments ARE the evaluation apps (O06); different task strings do not separate environments; the MoTiF slice (O07) is the only disjoint data and does not constitute held-out apps.

expectations.text: For memory/retrieval agents, show gains on environments other than those the memory was built from
expectations.applies_when: a claim that experience memory or retrieved trajectories improve GUI agents
expectations.reason: [both seats agree] sol: No independent environment outside constructed app memory. | son55: Gains of the memory are shown only on environments the memory was built from.

expectations.text: Compare observation modalities under the same backbone: accessibility tree / DOM only, screenshot only, screenshot + Set-of-Mark, screenshot + a11y tree
expectations.applies_when: a claim that a particular perception input or screen representation improves an agent
expectations.reason: son55 only (from domain card structured_screen_observation reviewer expectations); accepted: representation benefit not tested against other observation modalities.

claims.text: 90.9% action accuracy, 71.3% task completion with GPT-4; +36.4/+39.7 over GPT-4 LLM-framework
claims.setting: DroidTask 158 tasks/13 apps, teacher-forced, one reference trace, temperature 0.25, single run
claims.baseline/control: LLM-framework reproduced, same backbone; LLM-F scores 0 on Complete action (O10)
claims.selection_vs_test: memory built on the test apps (O06)
claims.allowed_conclusion: offline trace-agreement improvement on explored apps; not live task success or unseen-app automation

claims.setting: token counts, $/1000 queries, five-prompt latency, call reduction
claims.result/denominator: 625.3→339.0 tokens; 13.7% fewer calls; shortcut savings conditioned on correct shortcuts (O12)

assessment.author_claim_preserved: handles arbitrary tasks on any Android app without manual effort; 71.3% success rate
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On 158 DroidTask tasks in 13 apps that the system itself explored offline, AutoDroid prompting+memory exceeds a same-backbone LLM-framework prompt under offline single-trace matching and roughly halves prompt tokens. Live completion, unseen apps and isolated memory effect size are not established.

G.reason: Both seats 3; confirmed. Concrete bottlenecks (long trees, hidden navigation, query cost) with a named reproduced LLM baseline; lineage thin and residue toward live/unseen use not delimited.

M.reason: Both 3; confirmed. Onclick hints from the UTG directly target opaque intermediate steps; pruning targets length. Untested assumptions: exploration coverage and LLM summary correctness; no distinguishing prediction vs a naive memory dump.

X.reason: Both 3; confirmed. Algorithm 1, tags, merge rules, SFT recipe and offline costs reconstructable; k, gamma and exploration coverage unreported; failure boundaries only from 20 sampled failures.

E.measurement.reason: Decided for son55 (see resolution). The headline "success rate" is all-steps-correct agreement with one annotated trace (O01, O02), excludes the completion-determination step (O03), counts alternative valid paths as failures (O05), and authors withhold real-system completion (O04). Objective and defined, so not 0; but it does not measure the claimed task completion. Consistent with Auto-GUI where both seats gave 1 to a stronger (standard, tolerance-based, externally correlated) offline metric.

E.causality.reason: Both 2; confirmed. Same-backbone baseline and memory/CoT/MoTiF ablations exist; headline comparison changes representation, scrolling, output format and completion handling at once, baseline scores 0 on Complete (O10).

E.holdout.reason: Both 1; confirmed. Memory and SFT data come from exploring the same 13 test apps (O06); only the MoTiF slice is stated unrelated (O07); author-built benchmark; no unseen apps.

E.statistics.reason: Both 1; confirmed. Single run, temperature sensitivity of 2–4 points reported (O09), 20 sampled failures without totals, no intervals.

E.cost.reason: Both 3; confirmed. Tokens, $/1000 queries, on-device/cloud latency, call reduction and offline preparation reported against the same baseline; latency on five prompts only and shortcut savings conditioned on correct shortcuts (O12).

opus_initial_reading: Before seat ratings: system_method on Android with structure-tree input. Operation = offline random exploration of the SAME target apps → LLM-summarised simulated tasks/UI functions → retrieved into prompts (onclick hints) or distilled into a Vicuna SFT set; plus token pruning/merging and shortcuts. Evidence is offline: action accuracy and all-steps-correct "completion" against one human trace (O02), completion step excluded (O03), authors decline real-system results (O04). Baseline LLM-F scores 0 on the Complete action (O10). Memory/test apps identical (O06). Strongest supported: offline trace agreement gain and ~46% prompt-token reduction on 13 explored apps; claim_support scoped, evidence offline. The measure is defined/objective (not 0) but does not test the central task-completion claim. Cross-paper consistency: Auto-GUI’s standard AITW matcher, which has tolerance and an external human-correlation citation, received 1 from both seats.
